sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: State three key properties of a normal distribution's shape.
questions.answer: A normal distribution is: (1) symmetric and bell-shaped, centered at its mean; (2) unimodal (a single peak at the mean); (3) its total area under the curve equals \(1\), and it never touches the horizontal axis (it extends infinitely in both directions, getting closer and closer to zero).
questions.explanation: A normal distribution is: (1) symmetric and bell-shaped, centered at its mean; (2) unimodal (a single peak at the mean); (3) its total area under the curve equals \(1\), and it never touches the horizontal axis (it extends infinitely in both directions, getting closer and closer to zero).

questions.q: Explain what the two parameters \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) control in a normal distribution's shape.
questions.answer: \(\mu\) (the mean) controls the location of the center of the distribution (where the peak is). \(\sigma\) (the standard deviation) controls the spread: a larger \(\sigma\) produces a wider, flatter curve, while a smaller \(\sigma\) produces a narrower, taller curve — but both remain symmetric and bell-shaped.
questions.explanation: \(\mu\) (the mean) controls the location of the center of the distribution (where the peak is). \(\sigma\) (the standard deviation) controls the spread: a larger \(\sigma\) produces a wider, flatter curve, while a smaller \(\sigma\) produces a narrower, taller curve — but both remain symmetric and bell-shaped.

questions.q: Adult male heights are approximately normal with mean \(70\) inches and standard deviation \(3\) inches. Using the 68-95-99.7 rule, find the range of heights containing the middle 95% of adult men.
questions.answer: The 95% range spans \(\mu\pm2\sigma=70\pm2(3)=70\pm6\), so from \(64\) to \(76\) inches.
questions.explanation: The 95% range spans \(\mu\pm2\sigma=70\pm2(3)=70\pm6\), so from \(64\) to \(76\) inches.

questions.q: Events A and B are independent with \(P(A) = 0.49\) and \(P(B) = 0.12\). Find \(P(A \cap B)\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. Independence: \(P(A\cap B)=P(A)\cdot P(B)=0.49\times0.12=0.0588\).
questions.explanation: Independence: \(P(A\cap B)=P(A)\cdot P(B)=0.49\times0.12=0.0588\).

questions.q: Events A and B satisfy \(P(A) = 0.49\), \(P(B) = 0.37\), and \(P(A \cap B) = 0.16\). Find \(P(A \cup B)\).
Given \(P(A \cap B) = 0.32\) and \(P(B) = 0.8\), find \(P(A \mid B)\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. \(P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\dfrac{0.32}{0.8}=0.4\).
questions.explanation: \(P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\dfrac{0.32}{0.8}=0.4\).

questions.q: The graph shows the standard normal distribution (\(\mu=0\), \(\sigma=1\)), with the area to the left of \(z=1\) shaded (though shading itself is not shown, imagine it visually).
parts: Using \(P(Z<1)\approx0.8413\), find the area under the curve to the right of \(z=1\).
Explain, using the curve's symmetry, why \(P(Z<-1)=P(Z>1)\).
answers: The standard normal curve is symmetric about \(z=0\). By symmetry, the area to the left of \(-1\) is a mirror image of the area to the right of \(1\), so \(P(Z<-1)\) and \(P(Z>1)\) must be equal.
questions.answer: (a) \(P(Z>1)=1-P(Z<1)=1-0.8413=0.1587\).; (b) The standard normal curve is symmetric about \(z=0\). By symmetry, the area to the left of \(-1\) is a mirror image of the area to the right of \(1\), so \(P(Z<-1)\) and \(P(Z>1)\) must be equal.
questions.explanation: (a) \(P(Z>1)=1-P(Z<1)=1-0.8413=0.1587\).; (b) The standard normal curve is symmetric about \(z=0\). By symmetry, the area to the left of \(-1\) is a mirror image of the area to the right of \(1\), so \(P(Z<-1)\) and \(P(Z>1)\) must be equal.

questions.q: Explain how a normal probability plot (or normal quantile plot) can be used to assess whether a data set is approximately normal, and what a roughly straight-line pattern indicates.
questions.answer: A normal probability plot compares the ordered data values to what would be expected if the data were exactly normal. If the plotted points fall close to a straight line, the data is approximately normal. Systematic curvature or bending away from a straight line (such as an S-shape or clear bends at the ends) suggests the data deviates from normality — for example, skewness or heavy tails.
questions.explanation: A normal probability plot compares the ordered data values to what would be expected if the data were exactly normal. If the plotted points fall close to a straight line, the data is approximately normal. Systematic curvature or bending away from a straight line (such as an S-shape or clear bends at the ends) suggests the data deviates from normality — for example, skewness or heavy tails.

questions.q: Using the same pregnancy-length distribution and the 68-95-99.7 rule, find the approximate percentage of pregnancies lasting between \(234\) and \(298\) days.
questions.target: Applying the normal distribution to real data
questions.answer: \(234=266-32=\mu-2\sigma\) and \(298=266+32=\mu+2\sigma\), so this range spans \(\mu\pm2\sigma\). By the 68-95-99.7 rule, approximately \(95\%\) of pregnancies fall in this range.
questions.explanation: \(234=266-32=\mu-2\sigma\) and \(298=266+32=\mu+2\sigma\), so this range spans \(\mu\pm2\sigma\). By the 68-95-99.7 rule, approximately \(95\%\) of pregnancies fall in this range.

questions.q: A vending machine dispenses a soda whose volume is normally distributed with mean \(355\) mL and standard deviation \(4\) mL, independently of a snack bag whose weight is normally distributed with mean \(50\) g and standard deviation \(2\) g. If \(T\) represents the combined "total" formed by adding the soda volume (in mL) and snack weight (in g) as a single number, find the mean of \(T\). (This is a simplified illustrative combination, not a real physical unit.)
questions.target: Combining two independent normal random variables
questions.answer: For independent normal random variables, means add directly: \(\mu_T=355+50=405\).
questions.explanation: For independent normal random variables, means add directly: \(\mu_T=355+50=405\).

questions.q: Battery lifespans are normally distributed with mean \(500\) hours and standard deviation \(40\) hours. Find the \(z\)-score for a battery lasting \(460\) hours, and describe its relative position.
questions.target: Combining two independent normal random variables
questions.answer: \(z=\frac{460-500}{40}=\frac{-40}{40}=-1\). This battery's lifespan is exactly one standard deviation below the mean.
questions.explanation: \(z=\frac{460-500}{40}=\frac{-40}{40}=-1\). This battery's lifespan is exactly one standard deviation below the mean.

questions.q: The distribution of cholesterol levels in a population is approximately normal with \(\mu = 190\mathrm{\ mg/dL}\) and \(\sigma = 24\mathrm{\ mg/dL}\). (a) What proportion of individuals have cholesterol levels above 226 mg/dL? (b) What cholesterol level marks the 90th percentile?
questions.answer: (a) Proportion Above 226: Standardize: \(z = \frac{226 - 190}{24} = \frac{36}{24} = 1.50.\) Using standard normal tables: \(P(Z > 1.50) = 1 - 0.9332 = \mathbf{0.0668} \quad (6.68\%).\) (b) 90th Percentile: Find \(z^*\) such that \(P(Z < z^*) = 0.90\), which gives \(z^* \approx 1.282\). Unstandardize: \(x = \mu + z^* \sigma = 190 + 1.282(24) = 190 + 30.77 = \mathbf{220.77\mathrm{\ mg/dL}}.\)
questions.explanation: (a) Proportion Above 226: Standardize: \(z = \frac{226 - 190}{24} = \frac{36}{24} = 1.50.\) Using standard normal tables: \(P(Z > 1.50) = 1 - 0.9332 = \mathbf{0.0668} \quad (6.68\%).\) (b) 90th Percentile: Find \(z^*\) such that \(P(Z < z^*) = 0.90\), which gives \(z^* \approx 1.282\). Unstandardize: \(x = \mu + z^* \sigma = 190 + 1.282(24) = 190 + 30.77 = \mathbf{220.77\mathrm{\ mg/dL}}.\)

questions.q: A basketball player makes 75% of free throws. In a game, she shoots 12 free throws. Assuming attempts are independent: (a) Find the probability she makes exactly 9 free throws. (b) Find the mean and standard deviation of made free throws.
questions.answer: (a) Binomial PMF: \(X \sim B(n = 12, p = 0.75)\), \(k = 9\): \(P(X = 9) = \binom{12}{9} (0.75)^9 (0.25)^3 = 220 \times 0.075085 \times 0.015625 \approx \mathbf{0.2581}.\) (b) Mean & Standard Deviation: \(\mu = np = 12(0.75) = \mathbf{9.0\mathrm{\ free\ throws}}.\) \(\sigma = \sqrt{np(1-p)} = \sqrt{12(0.75)(0.25)} = \sqrt{2.25} = \mathbf{1.5\mathrm{\ free\ throws}}.\)
questions.explanation: (a) Binomial PMF: \(X \sim B(n = 12, p = 0.75)\), \(k = 9\): \(P(X = 9) = \binom{12}{9} (0.75)^9 (0.25)^3 = 220 \times 0.075085 \times 0.015625 \approx \mathbf{0.2581}.\) (b) Mean & Standard Deviation: \(\mu = np = 12(0.75) = \mathbf{9.0\mathrm{\ free\ throws}}.\) \(\sigma = \sqrt{np(1-p)} = \sqrt{12(0.75)(0.25)} = \sqrt{2.25} = \mathbf{1.5\mathrm{\ free\ throws}}.\)

questions.q: Consider a discrete random variable \(X\) that represents the number of heads obtained when a fair coin is tossed 3 times. The probability distribution of \(X\) is given by: What is the probability that \(X\) is less than 2, i.e., \(P(X < 2)\)? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.target: Standardizing and using the normal distribution
questions.answer: Final Answer: \(\frac{4}{8}\). The event \(X < 2\) for the discrete random variable \(X \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}\) consists of the outcomes \(X = 0\) and \(X = 1\). Adding their probabilities from the table gives: \(P(X < 2) = P(X = 0) + P(X = 1) = \frac{1}{8} + \frac{3}{8} = \frac{4}{8}.\)
questions.explanation: The event \(X < 2\) for the discrete random variable \(X \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}\) consists of the outcomes \(X = 0\) and \(X = 1\). Adding their probabilities from the table gives: \(P(X < 2) = P(X = 0) + P(X = 1) = \frac{1}{8} + \frac{3}{8} = \frac{4}{8}.\)

questions.q: Two independent random variables are normally distributed as \(X \sim N(50, 16)\) and \(Y \sim N(45, 9)\). Find the probability that \(X > Y\).
questions.answer: 1. Define the difference variable \(W = X - Y\). The condition \(X > Y\) is equivalent to \(W > 0\). 2. Since \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent normals, \(W\) is normally distributed: Mean: \(\mu_W = E[X] - E[Y] = 50 - 45 = 5\). Variance: \(\sigma_W^2 = \mathrm{Var}(X) + \mathrm{Var}(Y) = 16 + 9 = 25 \Rightarrow \sigma_W = 5\). Thus \(W \sim N(5, 25)\). 3. Compute \(P(W > 0)\): \(z = \frac{0 - 5}{5} = -1.0.\) \(P(W > 0) = P(Z > -1.0) = P(Z < 1.0) = \Phi(1.0) \approx 0.8413 \approx 0.841.\)
questions.explanation: 1. Define the difference variable \(W = X - Y\). The condition \(X > Y\) is equivalent to \(W > 0\). 2. Since \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent normals, \(W\) is normally distributed: Mean: \(\mu_W = E[X] - E[Y] = 50 - 45 = 5\). Variance: \(\sigma_W^2 = \mathrm{Var}(X) + \mathrm{Var}(Y) = 16 + 9 = 25 \Rightarrow \sigma_W = 5\). Thus \(W \sim N(5, 25)\). 3. Compute \(P(W > 0)\): \(z = \frac{0 - 5}{5} = -1.0.\) \(P(W > 0) = P(Z > -1.0) = P(Z < 1.0) = \Phi(1.0) \approx 0.8413 \approx 0.841.\)

questions.q: A data set has \(Q_1=17\) and \(Q_3=35\). Using the 1.5×IQR rule, which of the following values would be classified as an outlier?
questions.answer: IQR \(= 35-17 = 18\). Lower fence \(= 17 - 1.5(18) = -10\). Upper fence \(= 35 + 1.5(18) = 62\). The value -14 is below the lower fence, so it is an outlier.

questions.q: A researcher is designing an experiment to test the effectiveness of a new fertilizer on plant growth. They have a total of 50 experimental plots available. The experiment will involve two treatments: the new fertilizer (Treatment A) and a standard fertilizer (Treatment B). To ensure fair comparison and control for confounding variables, they decide to use a randomized block design. The plots are divided into 5 blocks based on soil quality, with each block containing 10 plots. Within each block, the plots will be randomly assigned to either Treatment A or Treatment B. If the number of plots assigned to Treatment A within the first block is \(x\), and the total number of plots assigned to Treatment A across all 5 blocks is 25, and the proportion of plots assigned to Treatment A in block 1 is \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the total plots in block 1, what is the value of \(x\)?
questions.target: Applying the normal distribution to real data
questions.answer: The problem describes a randomized block design. There are 5 blocks, and each block has 10 plots, for a total of 50 plots. The experiment uses two treatments: Treatment A (new fertilizer) and Treatment B (standard fertilizer). The total number of plots assigned to Treatment A across all 5 blocks is 25. The question states that the proportion of plots assigned to Treatment A in block 1 is \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the total plots in block 1. The number of plots in block 1 is 10. Therefore, the number of plots assigned to Treatment A in block 1, denoted by \(x\), is \(x = \frac{1}{5} \times 10 = 2\).
questions.explanation: The problem describes a randomized block design. There are 5 blocks, and each block has 10 plots, for a total of 50 plots. questions.q: A researcher is designing a survey to understand student opinions on campus dining. The researcher decides to select students from the student directory using a systematic random sampling method. If the student directory has a total of \(1500\) students, and the researcher decides to select every \(10\)th student, starting with a randomly selected student between 1 and 10, how many students will be in the sample?
questions.answer: The sample size is determined by dividing the total population size by the sampling interval. The total population size is \(1500\) students, and the sampling interval is \(10\). Therefore, the number of students in the sample is \(\frac{1500}{10} = 150\). The starting point between 1 and 10 ensures that the selection is random, but it does not affect the total number of students sampled.
questions.explanation: The sample size is determined by dividing the total population size by the sampling interval. The total population size is \(1500\) students, and the sampling interval is \(10\). Therefore, the number of students in the sample is \(\frac{1500}{10} = 150\). The starting point between 1 and 10 ensures that the selection is random, but it does not affect the total number of students sampled.

questions.q: A researcher wants to investigate the relationship between the type of pet owned (Dog, Cat, Fish) and the preferred music genre (Rock, Pop, Classical). They collect data and present it in a two-way table. If the table has 3 rows and 3 columns, what is the total number of cells in the table that represent a combination of pet ownership and music genre?
questions.answer: A two-way table is used to display the frequency distribution of two categorical variables. The number of rows corresponds to the categories of one variable, and the number of columns corresponds to the categories of the other variable. The total number of cells in the table is the product of the number of rows and the number of columns. In this case, the number of rows is 3 (representing Dog, Cat, Fish) and the number of columns is 3 (representing Rock, Pop, Classical). Total number of cells = Number of rows \(\times\) Number of columns Total number of cells = 3 \(\times\) 3 = 9. Each cell represents a unique combination of pet ownership and music genre, such as 'Dog' and 'Rock', 'Cat' and 'Pop', etc.
